summary: Fleet invitations either reach the new machine or fail loudly: auto routes around missing Fabric pairing, --send-fabric reports success only on confirmed delivery, and --code-file writes its 0600 file or exits non-zero

schema.detail: Join codes are unchanged. A code made without st-fabric-adapter carries the member's non-Fabric endpoints and no pairing data, which existing joiners already redeem.

rules.detail: Without st-fabric-adapter, --via auto leaves Fabric out and uses Tailscale or loopback endpoints; when only Fabric could carry the invitation, every delivery form refuses with the setup it needs before an invite is created. --send-fabric first checks that NAME is a trusted peer in fabric peers. An invite created but not delivered is revoked.

compatibility.detail: --send-fabric cannot be combined with --code-file or --code-only; such commands used to skip the Fabric send silently, so a script that passed both now fails instead of reporting an invitation it never sent. join --fabric-inbox now waits up to ten minutes for the code instead of failing at once. Older joiners still join with any code this build issues.

downtime.detail: No restart or migration is required.

manual.detail: No manual step. Fabric pairing still needs st-fabric-adapter and Fabric with --runtime-peers; without them, auto invitations go over the member's Tailscale or loopback endpoints, and a member that advertises only Fabric refuses to invite until they are set up.

recovery.detail: A failed delivery revokes its invite; issue a new one. The code is never printed by --send-fabric or --code-file.
